Subject: Evaluation follow-up: incident/RCAs & next validation steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same page: 

Summary of discovery items from our call:
- Primary use case: multi-tenant inference for their internal analytics feature, ~150 QPS average, burst to 2k QPS during reports.
- Most sensitive: audit logs + KV cache retention policy.
- Critical questions raised by security: example incident RCAs, escalation timelines, and how fallbacks function under region/network failures.

What we will send by EOD:
1) An evaluation matrix (attached) with baseline latency/cost assumptions and recommended test vectors.
2) A short set of anonymized incident RCAs and post-mortem timelines so your security team can validate our process.
3) A proposed validation plan for you: tail-latency soak, KV cache cold-start test, and failover swap.

Ask from you / StratusCloud:
- Please confirm whether your security team needs PDFs or would prefer a redacted ticket export (we can provide either).
- Proposed window for runbook walk + hands-on test: Tue/Wed next week (Nov 11–12) afternoon PT.

Attachments: 20251109-eval-matrix.xlsx (matrix + baseline), redwood-incident-examples.pdf (redacted RCAs).

High-level competitive note (from call): you’re evaluating HyperscaleX managed endpoints and CloudGen’s inference API. We’ll circulate a short incident/SLA comparison and highlight where Redwood’s routing + automatic fallback reduces blast radius during provider-level outages.

Next steps (owners):
- Tessa: send RCAs + evaluation matrix (today).
- Rishi: draft a one-page competitor incident comparison and call out support SLA differences.
- Alex / Priya: confirm security format preference and pick a test window.

Thanks — talk soon,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Tessa — thanks, useful summary. A couple quick replies: 

1) Security prefers redacted ticket exports (PDF) over narrative summaries — would be great if you can include timeline timestamps and customer impact classification.
2) Test window: Nov 12, 1–3pm PT works for our infra lead (Priya) and the security reviewer.
3) For the incident RCAs, can you include one example where an upstream cloud provider outage forced a regional failover so we can see the timeline and automated fallback behavior? HyperscaleX told us they route across regions but didn’t provide runbooks.

We’ll sign the mutual NDA (DocuSign link) once we have the redacted RCAs. Also copying our security mailbox.

Alex / Priya — jumping in with the short competitor incident matrix you asked for and a couple notes ahead of the test. Attached: competitor-rca-summary.docx which is a consolidated view from public post-mortems and our customer experience team. High-level: 

- HyperscaleX: multiple region-level incidents in the last 18 months; their public post-mortems show cross-region failover but a manual reconciliation step that extended recovery by 3–7 hours in two cases. SLA credit windows typically require support escalation and business-impact evidence.
- CloudGen: siloed control plane issues caused longer configuration drift; customers reported cache invalidation problems during rolling upgrades.
- Redwood: automated smart-routing + prefix KV caching reduced customer impact in the largest outage we had last year; automated fallback cut 99.9th percentile token latency by diverting eligible requests to a verified cold-standby model. RCA examples in redwood-incident-examples.pdf are redacted but include detailed timelines and post-incident action items.

A few practical notes for Nov 12 test: 
1) We'll run a controlled tail-latency test (1 hour) with a 10% failure injection to validate fallback behavior. Expect temporary increases in p50 but tails should stay within your SLOs.
2) For the KV cold-start, bring a representative prompt set and we’ll capture cold vs warm token counts.
3) We recommend you provide a short list of top 10 queries so we can emulate realistic cache hit patterns.

Attachments: competitor-rca-summary.docx

Rishi
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
